doc.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998

title: Joe Viola and getting a soprano saxophone
summary: Studying with Viola from age 12 or 13 led her to soprano; she still plays the Selmer he picked out.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you about when two things happened for you. First of all, the soprano saxophone — when did that become your instrument of choice?

Well you know I think I was studying with Joe Viola in Boston, a very fine saxophone teacher. And soprano was a passion of his. So I can remember him pulling it out during lessons and stuff. I started with him when I was about 12 or 13, so I was exposed to it quite young. And when I heard him play it, I liked that. I want to play like that.
Yeah, sure. And I’m sure I picked up a lot of love for the instrument from him. So I started studying with him I think I was 12 or so, 12 years old, 13, I think it was 12. So that’s when it began.
When were you able to get one?

Well I rented one early on. Then I remember I had a, I think it was a Czechoslovakian one, it was a Maadi or something. And then it didn’t take long before I wanted a Selmer. So I had got myself a Selmer alto and that took some time, then a Selmer soprano. Actually the instrument that he picked out for me, way back then, is the same one I’m playing. I mean I have other ones at home, I have three of them now, but that’s my main horn still.
